name: paranoia
quote: I'm afraid a poisonous spider will bite me at night.
description: A prediction not supported by evidence that a significant problem is likely to happen, causing stress and a desire to avoid the problem.
perceptions: There's no evidence, but I'm sure of it.

guidance.description: If you're experiencing paranoid thoughts, there are things you can do to help yourself cope. You may choose to try them on their own, or alongside treatment.

variations.name: debilitating paranoia
variations.description: Your life experience is significantly degraded by avoiding common activities due to fear of trouble not based on credible evidence.
perceptions: There's no evidence, but I'm sure of it.
I need to be more careful than others.
examples: He's so afraid of accidents, he won't leave the house

comparisons.description: People sometimes use the term 'paranoia' to just mean 'very anxious'. Anxiety is similar, but less stressful: you can be anxious when alert to a potential problem without losing sleep. Paranoia is amped up anxiety not warranted by the situation that drives inconvenient defensive actions.
Paranoia is more general, not always assuming that a shadowy group is going to cause a problem.

A 'phobia' is a fear of being exposed to something. Being 'paranoid' means you're constantly worried that the thing you fear is right around the corner. For example, you may have a phobia of spiders, but might not be paranoid about spiders getting in your luggage.

commentaries.quote: Success breeds complacency. Complacency breeds failure. Only the paranoid survive.

Many people defend 'paranoia' as being a motivator in business and life that encourages awareness and control. But what proponents are probably talking about is low-grade anxiety exaggerated to make a point. Paranoia is higher-grade anxiety that can't be turned off.
